sections.label: Extending EA core provisions
sections.summary: Core provisions of the EA will be extended to cover all managers and executives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: First, we will extend core provisions of the EA to cover all managers and executives.

sections.label: Removing salary threshold for managers
sections.summary: The $4,500 salary threshold for managers and executives will be removed, covering all employees under EA core provisions and benefiting 430,000 more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In consultation with the tripartite partners, we will remove the $4,500 salary threshold for managers and executives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In doing so, all employees, whether managers and executives, workmen or non-workmen, will be covered by core provisions under the EA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This will benefit an additional 430,000 managers and executives.

sections.label: Raising non-workmen salary threshold
sections.summary: The salary threshold for non-workmen will rise from $2,500 to $2,600, bringing Part IV employees to half the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In consultation with the tripartite partners, we will increase the salary threshold for non-workmen from $2,500 to $2,600, bringing Part IV employees to half of our total workforce.

sections.label: Amending EA deduction conditions
sections.summary: The EA will be amended to allow a deduction if it fulfils two conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The EA will be amended to allow a deduction if it fulfils two conditions.

sections.label: Shifting wrongful dismissal adjudication
sections.summary: Adjudication of wrongful dismissal claims will shift from MOM to the ECT for a one-stop service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To provide both employees and employers with a more convenient "one-stop service", we will shift the adjudication of wrongful dismissal claims from MOM to the ECT.

sections.label: Publishing wrongful dismissal guidelines
sections.summary: With the transfer to the ECT, MOM will publish Tripartite Guidelines on Wrongful Dismissal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With the transfer of the adjudication function to the ECT, MOM will publish a set of Tripartite Guidelines on Wrongful Dismissal.

sections.label: Recognising MCs from registered doctors
sections.summary: Employers will be required to recognise medical certificates from all registered doctors for granting paid sick leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Moving ahead, we will require employers to recognise MCs from all registered doctors for the purpose of granting paid sick leave.

sections.label: Hospitalisation versus home rest preference
sections.summary: A hospital doctor may assess that a pregnant woman needs hospitalisation for bed rest, though she may prefer resting at home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, a hospital doctor may assess that a pregnant woman requires hospitalisation for bed rest due to complications in pregnancy, but she may prefer to rest at home.

sections.label: Protecting employees from adverse employment practices
sections.summary: The EA will let the Minister for Manpower make regulations protecting employees, starting with civil contraventions for receipt-related practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The worker may not realise that salary vouchers can be used as proof of receipt of payment in cases of dispute.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, provide in the EA that the Minister for Manpower can make regulations to protect employees from any employment practice that may adversely affect their well-being, including where the enforcement of their entitlements might be at risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For a start, we intend to make it a civil contravention for employers to ask an employee to indicate receipt of salary before he is paid, or sign a receipt that is blank or inaccurate.

sections.label: PMET workforce share and EA coverage
sections.summary: PMETs are about 56% of the local workforce, expected to reach 65% by 2030, while the EA currently covers M&Es earning up to $4,500.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Today, our PMETs make up about 56% of the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: By 2030, that proportion is expected to increase to 65%.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Currently, the EA covers M&Es whose salaries are up to $4,500, to allow them to enjoy legal protection, including when it comes to sick leave, working on public holidays, and wrongful dismissal.

sections.label: Over 500,000 employees benefiting
sections.summary: More than 500,000 employees in total will benefit from these amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In total, more than 500,000 employees will benefit from these amendments.

sections.label: Including all PMEs under the Bill
sections.summary: The Bill includes all PMEs, extending key statutory benefits to an additional 430,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, the inclusion of all, I repeat, all professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is a watershed moment for Singapore's labour legislation and extends key statutory benefits to an additional number of 430,000 workers.

sections.label: Expanding EA to all PMEs
sections.summary: The speaker says he has lobbied since 2011 to expand the Employment Act to all PMEs, including those earning over $4,500 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I have been lobbying since 2011 for the expansion of the EA to cover all PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am glad we have moved the needle in 2014 and now to all PMEs, including those earning more than $4,500 a month.

sections.label: Removal of salary cap
sections.summary: Removing the salary cap raises employment standards by giving all workers core EA protection and access to the ECT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The removal of the salary cap signals the raising of employment standards in Singapore by according all workers with protection under the core provisions of the EA and with access to ECT.

sections.label: Higher salary cap for non-workmen
sections.summary: Raising the non-workmen salary cap to $2,600 and the Part IV overtime salary level to $2,600 will benefit over 100,000 non-workmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The increase in the salary cap for non-workmen from $2,500 to $2,600 and overtime rate payable for non-workmen from a salary level of $2,250 to $2,600 under Part IV of the Act will benefit more than 100,000 non-workmen.

sections.label: Retrenchment, dismissal claims, ECT
sections.summary: Employers must furnish retrenchment information if required by the Commissioner, and the ECT becomes a one-stop service for salary and wrongful dismissal claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Employers will have to furnish information on retrenchment of any employee, if they are required to do so by the Commissioner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Another enhancement is the transfer of adjudication of wrongful dismissal claims to the ECT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the passing of the Bill, the ECT will serve as a one-stop service for salary-related and wrongful dismissal claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Bill also provides that the ECT and the Labour Court are to have regard to the tripartite guidelines on wrongful dismissals when deciding any claim involving wrongful dismissals.

sections.label: Sick leave and quarantine changes
sections.summary: Amendments to section 89 make employers recognise outpatient sick leave certified by any medical practitioner, and quarantined employees are deemed hospitalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: (b) With the proposed amendments to section 89, the employer will recognise outpatient sick leave which is certified by any medical practitioner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: (c) With regard to infectious diseases, clause 15 provides that an employee who is under quarantine under any written law will be deemed to be hospitalised.

sections.label: Streamlined salary deductions consent
sections.summary: Clause 4 streamlines specified deductions and adds a catch-all for deductions with written employee consent, with a question on when consent must be obtained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Fifth, clause 4 of the Act has streamlined the list of specified deductions which an employer may make from the employee's salary and introduce a catch-all provision allowing employers to make any other deductions to which the employee has given written consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, to ensure that measures included in clause 4 to protect the employee are effective, could the Minister confirm that the written consent must be obtained from the employee at the point of time when the deduction is to be made, and the employers will not be deemed to have met this requirement through practices, such as incorporating clauses in employment contract stating that the employee agrees that the employer may make deductions as and when considered necessary.

sections.label: Lawyer declares interest, PMET coverage
sections.summary: A lawyer declares his interest and notes the Bill includes PMETs earning over $4,500 a month in the EA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I declare my interest as a lawyer who advises on employment law matters and disputes in my practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is good news that under this Bill, PMETs earning more than $4,500 a month will be included in the EA.

sections.label: Managerial executive claim service period
sections.summary: Clause 3(b) proposes reducing the prior service period from 12 to six months for managerial or executive claimants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For someone who is employed in a managerial or an executive position, clause 3(b) of the Bill proposes to reduce the prior period of service from 12 to six months before a claim can be lodged.

sections.label: ECA claim limits
sections.summary: Under the ECA, claims are limited to $20,000 or $30,000 for claimants using the Tripartite Mediation Framework or union-assisted mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, under the ECA, claims are limited to $20,000 or $30,000 for claimants who go through the Tripartite Mediation Framework or mediation assisted by their unions under the Industrial Relations Act.

sections.label: Tribunal limits, evidence, lawyer representation
sections.summary: The speaker asks about raising claim limits and raises concerns on evidence rules and lawyer representation at the Tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider raising the limits so that more disputes can be heard by the Tribunal?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I have previously spoken against the provision in the Employment Claims Bill which allows the Tribunal not to be bound by rules of evidence in the conduct of any proceedings where I pointed out that the risks of a tribunal failing to consider relevant evidence or making its decision based on arguably wrongful evidence cannot be discounted and this affects the quality of justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Employees have no right to have lawyers representing them at the ECT as the law does not allow representation by lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, I believe that the law does not expressly prohibit companies from using their inhouse legal counsel, who may be a fully qualified lawyer, to represent them at such proceedings.

sections.label: MOM ordered ex-gratia payment
sections.summary: Despite contractual provisions and disciplinary breaches, MOM told the company to give the employee an ex-gratia payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The employer could well have terminated the contract on disciplinary grounds, which would have meant that she would have been paid less upon termination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, contrary to the clear contractual provisions and despite the disciplinary breaches, the company was told by MOM to provide ex-gratia payment to the employee.

sections.label: Benefits extended to more workers
sections.summary: Extending these benefits to roughly 400,000-plus more workers is a step forward for labour welfare in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Extension of these benefits to roughly an additional 400,000-plus workers is, indeed, a step in the right direction for labour welfare in Singapore, a country strongly dependent on our human capital.

sections.label: Managers and executives coverage
sections.summary: After the amendments, all managers and executives except Part IV of the EA will be covered by the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Except for Part IV of the EA, all managers and executives will now be covered by the Act after the amendments are passed.

sections.label: Overtime costs for employers
sections.summary: Removing the $2,250 salary cap and raising the Part IV threshold to $2,600 would raise employer overtime costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, with the removal of the salary cap of $2,250 for overtime rate and raising of salary threshold to $2,600 in Part IV of the EA, employers would also be impacted by higher overtime costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, in the food and beverage (F&B) and accommodation services sector in which I operate, labour cost accounts for 42.8% of the operating cost, one of the highest amongst the different industries.

sections.label: PMET share of workforce
sections.summary: PMETs make up 56.1% of the local workforce and would rise to about 65% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: PMETs, who now make up 56.1% of the local workforce, would rise to about two-thirds, or 65%, by 2030.

sections.label: Section 14 dismissal amendment
sections.summary: Employers most concerned about the section 14 amendment, which lets all employees claim wrongful dismissal and cuts the service period to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, of all the proposed amendments, employers have most concerns with the section 14 amendment of the EA on dismissal, whereby all employees will be able to make a claim for wrongful dismissals following the proposed amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Moreover, the eligibility service period of managers and executives to claim for wrongful dismissal has been reduced from 12 to six months.

sections.label: Employer viewpoint and enforcement
sections.summary: An employer asks the Ministry to consider his suggestions and proposes an educational campaign with light-touch enforcement in the first year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin)   Mr Deputy Speaker, while many of the proposed amendments are not new obligations, as they merely extend benefits to a wider pool of workers, it is in and from the context of an employer’s viewpoint that I hope that the Ministry will consider my suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also verily believe that a focused educational campaign, together with a light-touch enforcement approach in the first year of the amendments, can be undertaken by the Ministry, together with its stakeholders, for the benefit of employers.

sections.label: Trade unions and productivity
sections.summary: Trade unions safeguard workers' interests, which requires productive companies, government infrastructure and stable conditions to attract investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our objective as trade unions is to safeguard the interests of workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We can do so effectively only if companies become more productive and competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government must continue to provide good infrastructure, transparent regulations and stable conditions to attract investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Then workers can continue to have good jobs and look forward to fair wage increases.

sections.label: Tripartite Partnership and EA amendments
sections.summary: The Tripartite Partnership has worked tirelessly and largely smoothened difficult amendments made to the EA over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, the Tripartite Partnership has worked tirelessly and largely smoothened the sometimes-difficult amendments made to the EA over the years and continue to do so.

sections.label: Salary threshold for non-workmen
sections.summary: The salary threshold for non-workmen rises from $2,500 to $2,600, a 4% increase since 2012, protecting 100,000 more non-workmen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While these amendments are a step in the right direction, I have a few concerns, especially in terms of reducing workers' vulnerability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I support the increase in the salary threshold for non-workmen that will provide them with additional protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The increase from $2,500 to $2,600 represents a 4% increase since the last salary threshold in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While this new salary threshold ensures 100,000 more non-workmen in Singapore will receive additional protection, I would like to ask why this salary threshold could not have been higher.

sections.label: CHAS for Workfare recipients
sections.summary: A suggestion for MOM to work with MOH to extend CHAS so all Workfare Income Supplement recipients get free outpatient treatment at Government polyclinics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Perhaps then, I would like to suggest to MOM to consider working with MOH to extend the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) scheme to enable all Workfare Income Supplement recipients to receive free outpatient treatment at Government polyclinics.

sections.label: Pay for rest day work
sections.summary: A suggestion that workers who work during rest days be paid the same salary rate regardless of who requested the work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: First, I would like to suggest that the workers who work during their rest days are paid the same rate of salaries, regardless of whether the work is being done at the request of the worker or his employer.

sections.label: Gig economy worker protection
sections.summary: Foreign workers' medical costs are settled by employers, free outpatient treatment is considered for Workfare-eligible workers, and plans to protect gig economy workers are asked about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is very different from foreign workers, whereby the employers are responsible for settling the medical costs of foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We can consider providing outpatient treatment for free to all workers who are eligible for Workfare Income Supplement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Third, I am concerned that many workers in the gig economy, like Grab drivers and delivery staff like Deliveroo workers, are not considered as workers under those employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What are the available plans to protect such workers from the gig economy?

sections.label: EA extension to managers and executives
sections.summary: The most significant improvement is the extension of core provisions of the EA to managers and executives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The most significant improvement is the extension of core provisions of the EA to managers and executives.

sections.label: Bill and labour market rigidity
sections.summary: Concerns that the Bill may increase labour market rigidity for managers and executives, though core EA provisions are basic labour rights.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are concerns that this Bill may increase labour market rigidity for managers and executives and, hence, reduce economic efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the core provisions of the EA, such as timely payment of salary, wrongful dismissal protection, and mandatory annual leave, are really basic labour rights.

sections.label: Self-employed private hire drivers
sections.summary: The Ministry's handout shows about one in 20 self-employed persons here are private hire drivers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Ministry's handout (Annex 4), just handed out before this debate, shows that about one in 20 of the self-employed here are private hire drivers.

sections.label: Contracting parties and statutory responsibilities
sections.summary: Many contracting parties want control over the self-employed but none of the statutory responsibilities under the EA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In short, many contracting parties want to have all the benefits of control over the self-employed, but none of the statutory responsibilities under the EA.

sections.label: Tripartite Standard and misclassification
sections.summary: The Minister noted the Tripartite Standard on Contracting with Self-Employed Persons was formed in March 2018, and clearer directions are sought.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a reply given yesterday to a Parliamentary Question I filed, the Minister for Manpower noted that the Tripartite Standard on Contracting with Self-Employed Persons was formed in March 2018 to better regulate this emerging area.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will ask the Minister if more clear directions can be set forth so that employers are not tempted to misclassify workers as self-employed as a means of evading the EA.

sections.label: EA amendment and TAFEP records
sections.summary: The EA amendment lets the Minister make regulations on undesirable employment practices, and publishing TAFEP case records is suggested.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The EA amendment will help by allowing the Minister to make regulations on some undesirable employment practices.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But, Sir, it will be useful if the Minister will consider making public the records of cases dealt with by TAFEP, so that the public can see that unfair practices are being addressed.

sections.label: EA salary cap removal
sections.summary: Removing the S$4,500 salary cap extends core EA provisions to 430,000 more managers and executives, and raising the non-workmen threshold to S$2,600 benefits 100,000 more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: According to MOM's Labour Force in Singapore 2017 report released on 26 January this year, PMETs make up more than half of our workforce, at 56%, up from 49% in 2007.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the increase in the number of PMEs, employees who earn more than S$4,500 per month will increase, and a key proposed amendment to the EA is the removal of the salary cap of S$4,500 for coverage of core employment provisions, such as minimum paid leave, public holiday and sick leave entitlement, allowable deductions, as well as the redress for unfair dismissal, contract termination and salary payment rights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This inclusion will ensure the provision of the basic and fair working conditions for all employees regardless of their salary levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This amendment is significant as it will mean the expansion of eligibility for PMEs and it translates to an additional 430,000 managers and executives who will be covered for the core provisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the proposed amendment to raise the salary threshold for non-workmen to S$2,600, Part IV of the EA, which covers rest days, hours of work, overtime pay and other conditions of service, will extend additional protection to more than half of the workforce and benefit 100,000 more non-workmen.

sections.label: Regulations on employer conduct
sections.summary: The amendment proposes regulations may regulate employer conduct to protect employees from practices adversely affecting their well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment of this Act proposes that such regulations may now, and I quote directly from the Bill, "regulate the conduct of an employer towards an employee, for the purposes of protecting the employee from any employment practice that may adversely affect the well-being of the employee".

sections.label: Violation as civil contravention
sections.summary: Clause 22(c) prescribes violation of regulations under proposed clause 22(a) as a civil contravention instead of an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On that, it therefore baffled me to learn that clause 22(c) of the Employment (Amendment) Bill prescribes any violation of the regulations to be implemented under the proposed clause 22(a) as a civil contravention, instead of an offence.

sections.label: Workplace stress and mental conditions
sections.summary: 90% of psychological conditions in Singapore adults have their root cause in workplace stress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Further, 90% of psychological conditions with adults in Singapore have their root cause in workplace stress.

sections.label: Migrant workers' mental illnesses
sections.summary: Over 60% of non-domestic migrant workers with outstanding injury and salary claims were predicted to suffer serious mental illnesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Over 60% of our non-domestic migrant workers who had outstanding injury and salary claims were predicted to be suffering from serious mental illnesses.

sections.label: Japan guidelines and NCSS study
sections.summary: Japan's non-binding mental health guidelines became standard practice, while an NCSS study found many Singaporeans unwilling to work with persons with mental health issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Japan, the government established the "Promotion and Maintenance of Mental Health of Workers" guidelines, which though not legally binding, have become a standard practice for employers in light of the social phenomenon of "karo-jisatu", commonly known as suicide from overwork.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a study conducted by the National Council of Social Service (NCSS), close to one in two Singaporeans were not willing to work with persons with mental health issues while 70% of employers agreed that negative attitudes of co-workers are major barriers to employing persons in recovery.

sections.label: Prohibiting early medical history enquiries
sections.summary: The Government should consider prohibiting employers from requiring job applicants to declare health conditions, similar to the UK's Equality Act 2010.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps, Mr Deputy Speaker, it would be a fair statement to say that the Government can and should, in line with the new direction and tone we are taking towards recognising employee well-being and encouraging inclusive employment practices, consider prohibiting to a reasonable extent, employers from requiring job applicants to declare their history of health conditions, be it physical or mental.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To my mind, such a balance could entail, for instance, prohibiting employers from making enquiries about an applicant’s medical history too early on in the recruitment process, much like what the UK has done in the Equality Act 2010.

sections.label: Non-workmen salary threshold increase
sections.summary: The salary threshold for non-workmen covered by Part IV additional protections would rise from $2,500 to $2,600.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The salary threshold for non-workmen to be covered by the additional protections of Part IV would be increased from $2,500 to $2,600.

sections.label: 2014 non-workmen salary threshold
sections.summary: In the 2014 amendment, the salary threshold for non-workmen was increased from $2,000 to $2,500.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the 2014 amendment, the salary threshold for non-workmen was increased from $2,000 to $2,500.

sections.label: Dismissal definition and forced resignations
sections.summary: The dismissal definition now covers forced resignations, closing a loophole, but the Bill does not define dismissal without just cause or excuse.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The definition of dismissal has been expanded to cover forced resignations, which plugs a loophole that employers could use to get around wrongful dismissal allegations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, this Bill misses the opportunity to define what constitutes dismissal "without just cause or excuse".

sections.label: Disguised or false retrenchment
sections.summary: A question asks whether wrongful dismissals would also cover disguised retrenchment or false retrenchment cases.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, I would like to ask if wrongful dismissals would also cover cases of disguised retrenchment or false retrenchment.

sections.label: PMEs, ECT claims and award cap
sections.summary: The EA will cover high-salaried PMEs who can bring wrongful dismissal claims to the ECT, but the Tribunal can award only up to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, with the passing of the Bill, the EA will cover high-salaried PMEs who would then be enabled to bring wrongful dismissal claims to the ECT.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, the Tribunal is limited to awarding claims up to only $20,000.

sections.label: Adjusting the award cap
sections.summary: A question asks whether the cap would be adjusted upwards after the amendment passes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the cap be adjusted upwards after the passing of this amendment?

sections.label: Workmen and non-workmen distinction
sections.summary: The speaker wants the workmen and non-workmen distinction removed and calls the $100 threshold increase too insignificant.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The first set has to do with the legacy distinction between workmen and non-workmen in providing for additional protections under Part IV of the EA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is my wish that the meaningless distinction be removed as soon as practicable and, in my view, the $100 increase in salary threshold for non-workmen eligible for the additional protections is too insignificant.

sections.label: Salary cap for white-collar workers
sections.summary: The speaker notes the proposed raise in salary cap for rank and file white-collar workers is only up to $2,600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As the median wage for employees continues to increase, rightly, so should the threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, I note that the proposed raise in salary cap for rank and file white-collar workers is only up to $2,600.

sections.label: Overwork, overtime pay and gig workers
sections.summary: The speaker raises employers giving empty titles to overwork staff, mandatory time-off after 10 hours, and gig worker protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Cases like this make me gravely concerned about employers who pay their junior staff a little higher than the salary threshold, even giving them an empty executive or managerial title, where they do not actually have executive or supervisory functions, so that they can legally overwork their employee without paying them overtime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Then there are professions, such as auditing and accounting, where pulling overnighters for days or even weeks to help clients to meet deadlines at certain periods of the year is inevitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I think that regardless of how much they are being paid, if they are required to work for more than 10 hours for the day, perhaps the EA should make it mandatory for them to be compensated with time-off, so they can rest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In addition, with the presence of more gig workers in the local labour market, I would like to ask the Minister how will they be protected under the enhanced EA?

sections.label: Timely hearing of cases
sections.summary: The speaker says cases should ideally be heard and resolved within six to eight months so victimised employees are not left hanging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Ideally, the cases should be heard and resolved within six months to eight months, otherwise it drags too long and the employee who is victimised is left hanging.

sections.label: Written consent for salary deductions
sections.summary: The speaker notes employers must now obtain written consent from employees before deducting salary for services like accommodation or amenities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Though less common, sometimes, it is the employee who tries to take advantage of the employer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I note that the employers are now required to obtain the written consent of their employees should they want to make any deductions from their salary for certain services, such as accommodation or amenities.

sections.label: Heavier penalties for errant employers
sections.summary: The speaker says errant employers should receive heavier penalties, especially if it is not their first dispute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Moreover, errant employers should receive heavier penalties, especially if it is not their first time facing a dispute.

sections.label: TAFEP powers against discriminatory employers
sections.summary: TAFEP has guided companies well, but the speaker hopes it gets more powers to penalise discriminatory employers more severely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: TAFEP has done a good job thus far in guiding companies to create an inclusive workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But I hope it can be given more powers to penalise discriminatory employers through more severe penalties.

sections.label: EA coverage for PMEs
sections.summary: The proposed amended Act's most significant change extends EA coverage to PMEs earning above $4,500 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The most significant change in the proposed amended Act would be extending the coverage of the EA to PMEs earning above $4,500 per month.

sections.label: Non-workmen salary threshold and overtime cap
sections.summary: Raising the non-workmen salary threshold and overtime rate cap to $2,600 covers half the workforce and benefits 100,000 more workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By extending the salary threshold for non-workmen to $2,600 a month and raising the overtime rate cap to $2,600 per month, it covers half of our workforce with additional protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The extension of the coverage of Part IV to cover more non-workmen will benefit another 100,000 more workers.

sections.label: Tripartite approach to retrenchment benefits
sections.summary: The speaker says retrenchment difficulties may be unavoidable, so a tripartite approach should issue an advisory on retrenchment benefit norms and support affected workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, it might not be avoidable when companies experience difficulties while restructuring or face financial crunch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, we should adopt the tripartite approach to instead: (a) issue an advisory stipulating the prevailing norms for retrenchment benefits quantum; and (b) support affected workers via programmes, such the Adapt and Grow and TechSkills Accelerator.

sections.label: Business environment and tripartism
sections.summary: A stable, transparent and conducive business environment draws company investment and better job prospects, and tripartism needs strong bipartism with Government support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A stable, transparent and conducive business environment has ensured that companies are willing to invest and set up business operations over here and thus ensuring better job prospects for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Tripartism can only succeed with strong bipartism between employers and unions with the support of the Government.

sections.label: Business transformation and employment law relevance
sections.summary: Businesses must transform and evolve, and the latest enhancements should continue so employment laws stay relevant, protecting workers while addressing business needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Businesses here must transform and evolve in order to sustain and grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is critical that these latest enhancements continue as part of our ongoing journey in ensuring our employment laws stay relevant and updated so that workers are protected while business needs are addressed.

sections.label: Unfair dismissal claim at ECT
sections.summary: Section 14(1) protects employees from unfair dismissal by allowing a claim to the ECT when dismissed without just cause or excuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 14(1) is intended to protect employees against unfair dismissal by allowing an employee to lodge a claim with the ECT where he has been dismissed without just cause or excuse.

sections.label: Deductions from employee salary
sections.summary: No deductions beyond a limited list may be made, but new section 27(1)(i) authorises any deduction made with the employee's written consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: No deductions beyond this limited list may be made from an employee's salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, this defined list seems to have been expanded by the new section 27(1)(i) which authorises any deduction made with the written consent of the employee.

sections.label: Deductions and foreign manpower statutes
sections.summary: The question asks whether new section 27(1)(i) remains limited by prohibited deductions under other statutes such as the EFMA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm that the new section 27(1)(i) remains limited by prohibited deductions under other statutes, such as sections 22A and 25(6) of the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (EFMA)?

sections.label: Written consent to salary deductions
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry tracks written consent and prevents coercion, and welcomes sections 27(1A) and (1B) on withdrawing consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry keep track of whether written consent has been obtained and how will the Ministry ensure that such written consent is not obtained coercively?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I welcome the new section 27(1A) and (1B) which clarifies that an employee cannot be penalised for withdrawing written consent to deductions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 27(1A) requires that the employee withdraw their consent any time before the deduction is made.

sections.label: Adverse inferences for missing evidence
sections.summary: New section 21(1A) lets the ECT draw adverse inferences when a party fails to produce evidence required under other written laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, the new section 21(1A) of the Employment Claims Act 2016 allows the ECT to draw adverse inferences where a party fails to produce evidence in breach of their obligation under other written laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can I confirm that this would mean that adverse inferences may be drawn against employers if they fail to produce Key Employment Terms and salary slips, which they are required to maintain under the EA?

sections.label: Work injury compensation doctor preference
sections.summary: The passage urges extending a principle to WICA and notes the first treating doctor's assessment is often preferred in permanent incapacity cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I would further urge the Minister to extend this principle to the work injury compensation regime in future reviews of WICA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that the assessment and diagnosis of the first treating doctor who is often also the doctor chosen by the employer is often preferred over doctors the employee may subsequently consult in the assessment of permanent incapacity under WICA.

sections.label: Removal of EA salary cap
sections.summary: The passage welcomes removing the $4,500 salary cap for EA protection, benefiting over 430,000 PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First and foremost, the move to do away with the $4,500 salary cap for protection under the EA is very much welcome.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This move will result in more than 430,000 PMEs who will benefit through greater protection under the EA.

sections.label: Annual leave of seven to 14 days
sections.summary: The passage supports providing all employees annual leave of seven to 14 days.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, I strongly support the move to provide all employees annual leave of seven to 14 days.

sections.label: Accepting MCs from registered practitioners
sections.summary: The passage welcomes accepting MCs from all medical practitioners registered under the Medical Registration Act for medical leave applications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Fourth, I welcome the move to accept MCs from all medical practitioners registered under the Medical Registration Act when employees apply for medical leave.

sections.label: Minister's regulations protecting employees
sections.summary: The passage welcomes a provision for the Minister to make regulations protecting employees' entitlements and well-being from undesirable employment practices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Fifth, I am heartened that within this round of amendments, there is a provision for the Minister to make regulations that protect employees' entitlements and well-being, and protect them from undesirable employment practices that manipulate, in particular, low-wage and menial work employees.

sections.label: Salary clawback cases and rank-and-file workers
sections.summary: The passage states reported cases are 0.2% of the workforce, about 8,300 annually, with over eight in 10 being rank-and-file workers subjected to salary clawback.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the number of cases reported accounts for only 0.2% of the workforce, the absolute numbers are about 8,300 cases annually, which is quite a substantial number.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am most concerned about the proportionately larger numbers of rank-and-file workers, more than eight in 10 of such workers, who have been subjected to this form of salary clawback.

sections.label: Rest spaces for outsourced personnel
sections.summary: The passage implores the Minister to consider mandating rest spaces for outsourced personnel like cleaners, despatch riders and security officers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Malay)   Still on the topic of protecting employees’ well-being, I would like to implore the Minister to consider making it mandatory for companies, organisations or buildings that conduct outsourcing of services, such as cleaning, delivery and security services, to provide proper rest spaces and areas for outsourced personnel, such as cleaners, despatch riders and security officers.

sections.label: Rest spaces for outsourced personnel
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to provide designated rest spaces for outsourced personnel in all buildings, organisations and companies hiring them, in the next EA amendment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A sheltered, well-ventilated and well-lit area with tables and chairs is all that is needed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Therefore, I implore the Minister for designated rest spaces and areas to be provided for outsourced personnel in all buildings, organisations and companies that hire such workers, in the next amendment to the EA.

sections.label: CPP practitioners issuing MCs
sections.summary: The speaker suggests allowing practitioners under the recently approved CPP framework to issue MCs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One such approach that I would like to suggest is to allow practitioners under the recently approved CPP framework to be able to issue MCs.

sections.label: Certifying CPPs and sick leave without MC
sections.summary: The speaker says MOM and MOH should consider certifying CPPs to issue MCs, and MOM should work with the Tripartite Alliance on three non-consecutive sick leave days without MC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The reasons I have stated provide sufficient grounds for MOM and MOH to consider certifying CPPs licensed to provide MCs to the general public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This brings me to my second point, which is, for MOM to consider working with the Tripartite Alliance and encourage employers to allow for up to three non-consecutive days of sick leave per year without MC.

sections.label: Sick leave without MC signals trust
sections.summary: Allowing employees up to three non-consecutive days of sick leave per year without MC would signal trust and partnership between employers and employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Allowing employees to take up to three non-consecutive days of sick leave per year without MC will also display a strong signal of trust and partnership between employers and employees.

sections.label: Jobs Central survey on faking illness
sections.summary: A 2012 Jobs Central survey reported that almost 20% of some 3,300 Singapore employees admitted to faking an illness to get away from work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A survey conducted by online portal Jobs Central in 2012 reported that almost 20% of some 3,300 Singapore employees admitted to faking an illness to get away from work at some point in time.

sections.label: Early therapy access and healthcare review
sections.summary: Overseas studies showed patients with musculoskeletal conditions benefited from early physiotherapy and occupational therapy, and the speaker urges reviewing the healthcare system while supporting the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Overseas studies have demonstrated that patients with musculoskeletal conditions, such as non-severe back or neck pain as well as hand injuries, benefited from early access to physiotherapy and occupational therapy at the primary care or emergency department.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we move into the ageing tsunami, there is an urgent need to proactively review our healthcare system and remove inefficiencies, making our processes leaner so that healthcare costs will not end up as a financial burden to our next generation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my requests stated above for MOM and MOH's consideration in future EA amendments, I stand to support the Bill.

sections.label: Income cap and overtime salary cap
sections.summary: The income cap for non-workmen under Part IV rises from $2,500 to $2,600, and the overtime salary cap rises from $2,250 to $2,600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, I welcome the move to raise the income cap for non-workmen under Part IV of the Act from $2,500 to $2,600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This provides coverage for an additional 100,000 non-workmen previously not protected on hours of work and overtime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Another piece of good news for workers is the proposed increase in the overtime salary cap for non-workmen from $2,250 to $2,600.

sections.label: Paid hospitalisation leave for infectious diseases
sections.summary: It asks whether employees with infectious diseases such as chicken pox and HFMD will be eligible for paid hospitalisation leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, will employees with infectious diseases, such as chicken pox and HFMD, be eligible for paid hospitalisation leave?

sections.label: Hospitalisation leave for mental issues
sections.summary: It asks the Minister to confirm that employees with mental issues can still qualify for hospitalisation leave under the proposed amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With the proposed amendment, can the Minister confirm that employees with mental issues can still qualify for hospitalisation leave?

sections.label: Chronic medical treatment and unfair employment practices
sections.summary: It suggests reimbursing chronic medical consultation fees and welcomes regulations against unfair employment practices such as signing blank salary vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Ministry can consider adding treatment of chronic medical issues as part of reimbursement of medical consultation fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Lastly, I welcome the move to allow the Minister to make regulations against certain unfair employment practices to protect employees’ entitlements and well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Foremost in mind, and as the Minister herself has highlighted earlier, would be to prohibit employers from asking employees to sign salary vouchers before receiving salaries or to sign on blank salary vouchers.

sections.label: Dealing with unfair employment practices
sections.summary: It states that companies and employers who flout this social norm and use unfair employment practices should be dealt with by the fullest extent of the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: On the same count, we expect companies and employers who flout this social norm and resort to unfair employment practices to be dealt with by the fullest extent of the law.

sections.label: EA coverage and part-time employee protection
sections.summary: It says the EA makes no distinction between temporary, contract, daily-rated or tenured employees, and that part-time employees working under 35 hours a week should know their protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The EA, and I quote from the MOM website, "does not make any distinction between a temporary employee, contract employee, daily-rated employee or employee on tenured employment".

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Employees working less than 35 hours a week should be made aware of the protection for them under regulations for part-time employees.

sections.label: Educating temporary contract daily-rated employees
sections.summary: The Ministry must reach out to and educate temporary, contract and daily-rated employees about overtime pay, wages, deductions, medical leave and dispute resolution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Whether it is overtime pay, timely payment of wages, salary deductions, medical leave or dispute resolution, the Ministry must make a concerted effort to reach out to and educate temporary, contract and daily-rated employees about their rights in these areas.

sections.label: Awareness helps workers negotiate
sections.summary: With greater awareness and knowledge, these workers can negotiate fairer terms and seek Ministry support when employers do not comply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In English): With greater awareness and more detailed knowledge, these workers will be able to negotiate for fairer terms of employment and seek support from the Ministry in the event of non-compliance by their employers.

sections.label: Employee groups needing MOM support
sections.summary: The speaker lists five employee groups MOM can further support: gig economy workers, outsourced functions, Baby Boomer Seniors, low-skilled elderly workers and employees with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The employee groups I hope MOM can further support are one, employees with a portfolio of jobs and employers in the gig economy; two, employees in outsourced functions; three, Baby Boomer Seniors; four, low-skilled elderly workers; and five, employees with disabilities.

sections.label: Update on portable benefits
sections.summary: The question asks the Ministry for an update on essential portable benefits such as healthcare, workmen's compensation and disability insurance not tied to full-time employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What is the update from the Ministry on essential portable benefits, such as healthcare, workmen's compensation and disability insurance that are not tied to traditional full-time employment?

sections.label: Re-examining CPF rates and contracts
sections.summary: The speaker says current assumptions to reduce CPF rates and continue year-on-year contracts subject to employer offers need to be re-examined.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The current assumptions to reduce Central Provident Fund (CPF) rates and to continue with year-on-year contracts subject to employer offers, I think, need to be re-examined.

sections.label: Special Employment Credit for elderly disabled
sections.summary: The Special Employment Credit incentivises employers to hire more elderly and disabled people, but many still require support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Special Employment Credit by the Government is a brilliant way to incentivise employers to hire more of these elderly and disabled but there are still many out there requiring support.

sections.label: Singapore UNCRPD signing and ratification
sections.summary: Singapore signed the UNCRPD in November 2012 and ratified it in July 2013, committing to protect rights of persons with disabilities in areas like education and employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Singapore has signed the UNCRPD on 30 November 2012.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Convention was later ratified in July 2013.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: By ratification, Singapore is committed to ensuring that the rights and interests of persons with disabilities will be protected like the rest of the population in key areas, such as education and employment.

sections.label: Australian public service disability targets
sections.summary: Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland set public service disability employment targets of 6% to 7% under an economic participation plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In Australia, the Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland governments have set public service disability employment targets of 6% to 7% as part of an economic participation plan for persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Employment Act amendment proposals
sections.summary: Proposals include removing the $4,500 salary cap, raising the non-workmen overtime salary cap from $2,250 to $2,600, benefiting 100,000 workers, while the workmen cap stays at $4,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Proposals, such as the removal of the monthly salary cap of $4,500, additional protection for more vulnerable employees and improvements to dispute resolution services, are greatly welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the amendments is to increase the salary cap for paying overtime to non-workmen from $2,250 to $2,600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is expected to benefit an additional 100,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On the other hand, the cap for workmen has been left unchanged at $4,500, since about 99% of workmen are already covered under this threshold.

sections.label: Employment Act purpose
sections.summary: The EA regulates employment practices in a balanced way, protecting workers while retaining labour market flexibility for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The EA exists to regulate employment practices in a balanced way, protecting workers while retaining labour market flexibility for businesses to thrive and create good jobs.

sections.label: Employer obligations paternity re-employment
sections.summary: Employers have been asked to take on more obligations such as longer paternity leave and re-employment of older workers to 65 then 67.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Fourth, in recent years, employers have been asked to take on more obligations, such as longer paternity leave and re-employment of older workers, first to 65 then to 67.

sections.label: Salary thresholds workmen non-workmen
sections.summary: The $4,500 threshold covers nearly all workmen while the non-workmen threshold covers about half, with intent to close the gap.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The salary threshold of $4,500, therefore, covers nearly all workmen, whereas the salary threshold for non-workmen covers about half of them.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our longer-term intent is, indeed, to close the gap between the salary thresholds for workmen and non-workmen.

sections.label: EA coverage for managers and executives
sections.summary: Tripartite partners agreed to extend EA core provisions to all managers and executives, covering about half a million workers in total.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In this amendment, the tripartite partners agreed to the major shift to extend EA core provisions to cover all managers and executives.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The expanded coverage under Part IV benefits another 100,000 or so workers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, in total, we are talking about half a million.

sections.label: Interventions on wrongly classified SEPs
sections.summary: Over three years, around 100 cases of employees wrongly classified as SEPs were intervened in, helping them recover statutory benefits or CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the last three years, we have successfully intervened in around 100 cases where employees were wrongly classified as SEPs and helped them to recover their due statutory benefits or CPF contributions.

sections.label: Recognising medical certificates from any doctor
sections.summary: The EA amendments require employers to recognise medical certificates from any doctor, private or public, for granting paid sick leave.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The amendments to the EA in this Bill will require employers to recognise MCs from any doctor, whether private or public, for purposes of granting paid sick leave.

sections.label: Paid hospitalisation leave and outpatient entitlement
sections.summary: Employees with infectious diseases certified ill enough to be hospitalised get paid hospitalisation leave, and the 14-day outpatient entitlement covers most employees.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: An employee who has chickenpox or other infectious diseases, and who is hospitalised or certified by a hospital doctor to be ill enough to be hospitalised, will be granted paid hospitalisation leave, even if he is not physically warded.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The 14-day entitlement for outpatient medical treatment is sufficient to cover the vast majority of employees today, given that the average number of days of sick leave taken is 4.8 days.

sections.label: Written consent for deductions
sections.summary: Written consent cannot be a general contract clause letting an employer make any deduction as and when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Patrick Tay asked about written consent.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Such consent cannot be a general clause in a contract stating that an employer can make any deduction as and when necessary.

sections.label: Dismissal without just or sufficient cause
sections.summary: Dismissal is without just or sufficient cause if on grounds such as discrimination, denial of statutory benefits, or intent to punish employees for exercising rights.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The dismissal is without just or sufficient cause if it was on grounds, such as discrimination, denial of statutory benefits, and with the intent to punish the employees for exercising his rights.

sections.label: Wrongful dismissal claims limits
sections.summary: Wrongful dismissal claims have separate limits of $20,000, or $30,000 for union-assisted cases, in addition to salary or benefit claims.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To clarify, for wrongful dismissal claims, there will be a separate claims limit of $20,000 and $30,000 for union-assisted cases, in addition to the claims limit for any salary or benefit owed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, in other words, it can be up to $40,000 or $60,000, if the two are combined.

sections.label: Employment laws adverse inferences
sections.summary: A new Fourth Schedule in the Employment Claims Act will specify the employment laws ECT can draw adverse inferences from.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The list of employment laws that ECT can draw adverse inferences from will be specified in a new Fourth Schedule in the Employment Claims Act.

sections.label: Tripartite Standard self-employed persons
sections.summary: The Tripartite Standard on Contracting with Self-Employed Persons shapes norms, and MOM will review the EA and strengthen SEP support.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Tripartite Standard on Contracting with Self-Employed Persons also helps to shape norms and ensure the sustainability of the economy of self-employed work.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MOM and our tripartite partners will continue to keep a close watch on workplace trends like the ones that were mentioned and also others, for example, automation and flexible work arrangements, which Mr Saktiandi Supaat spoke extensively about.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will continually review the EA to ensure it stays relevant in regulating employment practices in a balanced way, protecting the rights of workers while retaining flexibility in the labour market for businesses to thrive.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I would add further that the right approach may need adjustments beyond the EA which is, indeed, the reason we aim to strengthen support for SEPs through the recommendations that I circulated.

sections.label: Implementing changes expeditiously
sections.summary: The focus is now on getting the changes implemented expeditiously and smoothly.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Let us now focus on getting the changes implemented expeditiously and smoothly.

sections.label: No mandatory retrenchment payouts
sections.summary: MOM and tripartite partners agree legislating mandatory minimum retrenchment payouts would be counter-productive.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MOM agrees with the tripartite partners on the need to strike a balance and that it would be counter-productive to try and legislate mandatory minimum payouts in the event of retrenchment.

sections.label: Advisory on retrenchment benefits
sections.summary: The US and Switzerland do not mandate retrenchment benefits, so tripartite partners issued an advisory on prevailing retrenchment benefit norms.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, countries like the US and Switzerland also do not mandate retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, given these considerations, the tripartite partners have issued instead an advisory stipulating the prevailing norms for retrenchment benefits quantum that employers should take into consideration when determining the retrenchment benefits.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits survey findings
sections.summary: A survey found about 90% of establishments that retrenched workers paid retrenchment benefits, with 70% meeting or exceeding prevailing tripartite advisory norms.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: According to our survey last year, around 90% of the establishments which retrenched workers actually paid retrenchment benefits even though there was no stipulated mandatory payout, of which 70% paid retrenchment benefits that met or exceeded the prevailing norms articulated in the tripartite advisory.

sections.label: Amendments to clause 15
sections.summary: Proposed amendments to clause 15 clarify that section 89(3) covers quarantine orders, non-inpatient hospitalisation, and post-discharge medical treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The amendments proposed to clause 15 improve the language in the law to make clear the intention for section 89(3) of the Act on Hospitalisation to cover the circumstances I had set out in my Second Reading speech, including quarantine orders, situations where the employee is not an inpatient of a hospital but is ill enough to require hospitalisation during that period, and further medical treatment for the condition that the employee was hospitalised for after discharge from hospital.
